clue.text: Answer after president's given short shrift

indicators.note: after puts the answer word behind the shortened president
short means the president's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln, the US president
an answer to a puzzle is its solution

explanation.surface: A president's reply to someone is curt and dismissive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short shrift' reads as one idiom, but 'short' trims ABE to AB and 'shrift' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrift is an old word for confession and the priest's forgiveness that follows it.

clue.text: Carriage fetched almost a million

indicators.note: almost means the word for fetched is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: fetched means brought
taken as written

explanation.surface: A carriage was sold for nearly a million at auction.
explanation.definitionFit: A brougham is a light four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage with an enclosed body.

clue.text: Regularly jovial and crude?

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of jovial, starting from the second

explanation.surface: Someone is cheerful and coarse in equal measure.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude is unrefined petroleum; the question mark flags this as an example-style definition.

clue.text: Superior meal, but no starter

indicators.note: no starter means the meal word loses its first letter, with a nod to a menu's first course

parts.note: supper is an evening meal

explanation.surface: An excellent dinner, though without a first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no starter' pretends to be the menu's first course but drops the first letter of SUPPER.
explanation.definitionFit: Upper and superior both describe a higher rank or position, as in the upper classes.

clue.text: What batsman off the mark might say is an art form

parts.note: what a batsman says of himself begins I am, shortened to two letters
off in the sense of away from or beyond, i.e. past
the starting mark in cricket is nought, the round letter O

explanation.surface: A cricketer's remark turns out to describe a kind of art.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman is 'off the mark' on scoring the first run, so could say I'M PAST O (nought); run together, that phrase gives the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Impasto is a painting technique of laying paint on thickly so brush or knife marks stand out.

clue.text: One breaks new organ playing Grieg?

definitions.note: an example of a person from Norway, so a noun

indicators.note: breaks means the single letter splits the shuffled letters
playing suggests the letters of new organ performing in a new order

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Someone plays a newly installed organ, performing Grieg.
explanation.definitionFit: Edvard Grieg, composer of Peer Gynt, was born in Bergen and is a famous national of Norway.

clue.text: Cook with mum, making bread

parts.note: to do food is to cook it, as in 'done to a turn'
mum means silent, and sh is the call for silence

explanation.surface: Baking with your mother to produce a loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bread' and 'Cook' suggest a bakery; bread is slang for money, and 'mum' is the quiet word, not mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread and dosh are both British slang for money.

clue.text: Unkempt beauty partied topless

parts.note: a dish is slang for an attractive person

indicators.note: topless means the word for partied loses its first letter, at the top in a down answer

parts.note: partied means revelled

explanation.surface: A good-looking person looks scruffy after partying without a top.
explanation.definitionFit: Unkempt and dishevelled both describe untidy hair or clothes.

clue.text: Maybe private bar one gets to join

indicators.note: bar means except, so the soldier word goes without the letter for one

parts.note: a private is an example of a soldier
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A private soldier, all but one, is allowed to enlist.
explanation.definitionFit: To solder is to fuse metal parts together, so it means to join.

clue.text: I'll go into lounge with champagne and a sweet

indicators.note: go into means the letter is placed inside the pair of words

parts.note: to loll is to lounge
pop is slang for fizzy drinks such as champagne
the I of I'll, which will go in

explanation.surface: Someone plans to relax with champagne and a dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: A lollipop is a hard sweet on a stick.

clue.text: Some furores ultimately ensue

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Outrage will eventually follow.
explanation.definitionFit: To result is to follow as a consequence, the same as to ensue.

clue.text: After university, English girl somehow is more unattractive

indicators.note: after puts the shuffled letters behind U
somehow says the letters come out in some new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An English girl loses her looks after going to university.
explanation.definitionFit: Uglier is the comparative of ugly, meaning less attractive.

clue.text: Embellished being badly treated outside restaurant

indicators.note: outside means the treatment phrase sits around the eatery word

parts.note: ill-used means badly treated
a trat is short for trattoria, an Italian restaurant

explanation.surface: A diner was roughed up outside a restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: An illustrated book is decorated with pictures, i.e. embellished.

clue.text: Starts to regret eating stuffing coloured like a kebab?

indicators.note: stuffing means the initials are packed inside the biased word

parts.note: coloured means biased, and skewed means biased too

indicators.note: starts to means the opening letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: Someone regrets eating a kebab, with its red-coloured stuffing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coloured' seems part of the kebab picture, but it means biased (SKEWED), and 'eating' only supplies a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Kebab meat is threaded on a spit, so it is pierced through like the pieces on a skewer.

clue.text: Punishment constrains everyone in revolutionary group to conform

indicators.note: constrains means the penalty word holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a fine is a monetary punishment
all means everyone
taken as written

indicators.note: revolutionary means the word for group is turned round

parts.note: a lot is a group, as in 'that lot'

explanation.surface: A revolutionary group are all penalised until they toe the party line.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall into line is an idiom for obeying the rules like everyone else.

clue.text: Small English bloke twice turns up to identify culprits

indicators.note: turns up in a down answer means the pieces read from the bottom upwards
twice means the pair of pieces is written two times

parts.note: a bloke is a man

explanation.surface: A little English man keeps showing up to point out wrongdoers.
explanation.definitionFit: To name names is an idiom for revealing who is guilty, especially to the authorities.

clue.text: Cuban perhaps lends air to dance

indicators.note: dance says the letters of lends air jig about into a new order

explanation.surface: A Cuban gives atmosphere to a dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuba is an island, so a Cuban is an example of an island inhabitant.

clue.text: As I'm left in penultimate part of contest, I could be this

definitions.text: As I'm left in penultimate part of contest, I could be this

indicators.note: could be says the gathered letters might become something else once rearranged
penultimate part of means the next-to-last letter of contest

explanation.surface: A contestant still standing in the round before the final reflects on their status.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' shuffles AS I'M LEFT IN with S, the next-to-last letter of 'contest', and the second I; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor who has reached the next-to-last round of a knockout tournament has this title.

clue.text: Silly John gets upset in school?

indicators.note: in means the turned word sits inside the shoal word

parts.note: a school of fish, hence fish; the question mark flags the odd sense

indicators.note: gets upset in a down answer means the word is turned upside down

parts.note: john is slang for a toilet, as is loo

explanation.surface: John is distressed at school and acts foolishly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' looks like a person but is the toilet; 'school' is a group of fish, not a place of learning.
explanation.definitionFit: Silly and foolish are synonyms for lacking good sense.

clue.text: I eat after ten

definitions.note: I is the chemical symbol of the element

indicators.note: after puts the meal word behind the number

parts.note: ten is written 10, which looks like the letters I and O
to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: Someone has dinner late, after ten o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' looks like the speaker but is the chemical symbol for the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The element with atomic number 53 has the chemical symbol I.

clue.text: Italian town that's no resort? Wrong!

indicators.note: wrong says the letters of no resort are set out in a wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone denies a famous Italian holiday spot is a resort and is corrected.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on the town actually being a well-known resort, hence 'Wrong!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorrento is a town on the Bay of Naples in Campania, southern Italy.

clue.text: Screw around and do sketch again?

indicators.note: around means the prison word is turned round

parts.note: screw is British prison slang for a warder or prison officer

explanation.surface: Messing about and then drawing the picture again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screw around' reads as fooling about; 'Screw' is a prison officer in British slang and 'around' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: To redraw is to draw again, as with a revised sketch.

clue.text: Consumed by fury, nanny's heading for a row

indicators.note: consumed by means the initial is swallowed by the anger word

parts.note: rage means fury

indicators.note: heading means the first letter of nanny's

explanation.surface: A furious nanny goes off to have an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' suggests an argument, which fits the fury, but it means a line, as in a range of hills.
explanation.definitionFit: A range is a line or series of things, such as a mountain range, so it is a row.

clue.text: Police returned, requiring corporation to make formal statement

indicators.note: returned means the police abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police
corporation is an old jokey word for a pot belly, a tum

explanation.surface: Police came back, needing a company to put out an official statement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' suggests a business but is old slang for a paunch.
explanation.definitionFit: A dictum is an authoritative pronouncement or maxim.

clue.text: Hint pub needs to open around middle of September

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: around means the opening word wraps the central letter

parts.note: to undo something is to open it

indicators.note: middle of means the central letter of September

explanation.surface: A pub is told to open in mid-September.
explanation.definitionFit: An innuendo is an indirect, often suggestive remark that hints rather than says.

clue.text: Be upset — boat's beginning to sink

indicators.note: upset in a down answer means the two letters are turned upside down
beginning means the first letter of boat's

explanation.surface: Don't fret: the boat has started going under.
explanation.definitionFit: To ebb is to decline or recede, as a tide or fortunes sink.

clue.text: Runs, wearing Edward's anorak

indicators.note: wearing means the name has the cricket letter on it, around it

parts.note: Ned is a pet form of Edward
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone goes jogging in Edward's waterproof jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anorak' looks like a coat to be worn, but it is British slang for an obsessive enthusiast.
explanation.definitionFit: Anorak is British slang for a socially awkward obsessive, the same as a geek.

clue.text: Randomly chosen composer — this one?

indicators.note: randomly says the letters of chosen are put in a random order

parts.note: Alban Berg was an Austrian composer

explanation.surface: Pick a composer at random: could it be this one?
explanation.walkthrough: Berg was a pupil of the answer, and the whole clue also describes a composer picked at random.
explanation.definitionFit: Arnold Schoenberg was the Austrian composer who devised twelve-tone music.
